what: The full photo panel ripples along a distortion map (strength -0.07, the front image rotated 360° and the back image 180°) and melts into the next photo over 3s with power4.out (WebGL). The progress line (--fx-progress) fills over 6s with power3.out, pivoting on the left, and while changing it drains backwards over the same 3s, pivoting on the right. The title panel slides out 3vw to the right and disappears (1.5s), and the new title enters from -1.5vw .17s later (1.5s), while the page number rolls one step over 2s. The prev and next buttons wind the running progress to its end at remaining share × 10 speed and then switch immediately

options.hold: Hold time per slide (sec, time for the progress line to fill), default 6
options.speed: Switch duration (seconds), default 3 — titles take half of this each
options.delay: Time (s) before progress first starts, default 0 — with a loader, the loader’s length
options.ease: Easing curve, in the form ”0.16,1,0.3,1” or a GSAP name, default power4.out
options.ratio: Image height-to-width ratio, default from the first image (.5 for a placeholder)
options.[data-fx-part=stage]: Surface the canvas is laid on (the element itself if none)
options.[data-fx-part=image]: Multiple images — img·canvas, or placeholders with data-label (painted with skin color blocks)
options.[data-fx-part=title]: Title panel that changes with each picture (optional)
options.[data-fx-part=reel]: Number slot on the rolling side (optional)
options.[data-fx-part=total]: Total number of chapters (01 format, optional)
options.[data-fx-part=bar]: Progress line — fx.css applies scaleX through --fx-progress and --fx-origin

from.where: index.html hero (.dd-kv) — the original script.js KV (ShaderMaterial dispFactor · intensity -.07 · changeSpeed 3 · power4.out · Elapse 6s · Reel 2s · Title 3vw/-1.5vw)

note: The original shader reads screen coordinates as gl_FragCoord×0.5, so it is only correct on screens with a pixel ratio of 2. Here the panel coordinate (uv) is multiplied by the cover ratio so the same picture appears on any screen. The distortion map is a hand-drawn wave noise. Progress pauses when off screen and resumes on return. With reduced motion only the first picture stays, and pressing the button switches it immediately
